info.title: Zouriel Workflows REST API
info.description: The API every engine serves under its mount point (MapWorkflowApi in .NET). Exported from the .NET sample app (GET /openapi/v1.json); paths are shown mounted at /api/workflows. Request and response bodies for definitions, registries and settings follow spec/schema/*.json.

post.description: The body is a workflow definition (spec/schema/definition.schema.json).

put.description: The body is a workflow definition (spec/schema/definition.schema.json).

post.description: The body is a workflow definition (spec/schema/definition.schema.json).

get.description: Items the caller may not see (IWorkflowAccessPolicy) are left out of `items` and of `total`, and `skip`/`take` count visible items. With a restrictive policy the server checks at most the first 5000 matches; past that, `total` also counts the unchecked rest.

Items the caller may not see (IWorkflowAccessPolicy) are left out of `items` and of `total`, and `skip`/`take` count visible items. With a restrictive policy the server checks at most the first 5000 matches; past that, `total` also counts the unchecked rest.

What a reset would take back (spec §6): the reset option and the items, oldest first, with a `token`. Item kinds: `created`, `field`, `action`, `message`, `webhook`, `move` (another record moved by applyTransition; never undoable). 403 `notAllowed` when the caller is not among the lifecycle's reset `who` or there is nothing to reset.

post.description: Starts the record's workflow over (spec §6). `undo` lists item ids to take back; `token` (from GET) makes the reset fail with 409 `resetChanged` when the list has changed since it was opened, as does an id no longer listed. 400 `notUndoable` for an item that cannot be taken back, `invalidInput` for the form. Writes that take things back start no automations.

key.description: The field key token paths use.

options.description: The options of an enum field.

lifecycle.description: True lets a lifecycle own it (enum fields only).

sensitive.description: True masks its values in audit, views and test runs.

required.description: True when the app requires a value.

FieldDescriptor.description: A field of an entity and what workflows may do with it (spec §2 flags).

label.description: The text shown to people (and rendered by templates).

FieldOption.description: One option of an enum field.

state.description: The state key to move to.

lifecycle.description: Which lifecycle, when the entity has more than one.
Which lifecycle, when the entity has more than one.

title.description: The definition's title in the pinned version.

version.description: The definition version the instance is pinned to.

kind.description: One of InstanceKinds: automation, record or run.

parentId.description: For child runs and waited-for sub-workflows: the instance that started it.

reason.description: For runs: which list it runs (`transition:ID`, `onEnter:ID`…); for sub-workflows, the parent step.

entity.description: The record type the instance is about, if any.

entityTitle.description: The record's title (its registry title field), when it can be read.

state.description: For record instances: the current state key.

error.description: The error of the incident (or failure) the instance shows.

errorStepId.description: The step that failed, for that incident.

initiatorId.description: The person who started it (null for system starts).

steps.description: The executed steps, oldest first (single-instance reads only).

tokens.description: The interpreter's threads and what each waits for (single-instance reads only).

outputs.description: Step outputs by step id, masked (single-instance reads only).

variables.description: The workflow variables, masked (single-instance reads only).

InstanceView.description: An instance (automation run, lifecycle record instance or child run), as the API and run viewer show it. Data is masked (spec §11).

LabelledItem.description: A key with a label, for channels, roles and groups.

code.description: Stable problem code, the same in every engine and editor (`spec/fixtures/lint`).

node.description: The id of the step, state or transition the problem is on; null for the whole definition.

message.description: What is wrong, in plain words.

LintProblem.description: One problem in a definition. `Node` is the id of the step, state or transition it is on.

oneOf.description: The form to fill in first, if any.

ManualOption.description: A manual-trigger workflow the viewer may start from a record (spec §5 `manual`).

edit.description: Create and edit drafts, validate, test runs, read settings.

publish.description: Publish, archive, restore, roll back and delete.

settings.description: Change global settings and purge the audit log.

intervene.description: Cancel, retry, skip, migrate, force state, reassign.

audit.description: Read and verify the audit log.

MePermissions.description: What the caller may do, one flag per policy of WorkflowApiOptions (true when no policy is set).

type.description: `user`, or `anonymous` when the API allows callers who are not signed in.

can.description: Which kinds of operation they may perform.

MeResponse.description: Reply of `GET /me`: the signed-in actor and what the API's policies let them do.

stateMap.description: Old state key → new state key, where keys differ.

total.description: How many items match in all.

PageOfInstanceView.description: One page of a list, with the total number of matches.

total.description: How many items match in all.

PageOfTaskView.description: One page of a list, with the total number of matches.

key.description: The key steps and tokens use.

required.description: True when an action input must have a value.

options.description: The options of an enum parameter.

entity.description: For relation parameters: the related entity's key.

ParamDescriptor.description: An input or output of an action, or a data field of a signal.

node.description: A transition id, `reset`, `trigger` (a manual start) or an approval/task step id.

who.description:
The assignees (roles, groups, users, person fields of the record) who may do it. What empty means depends on
the node: a transition or the reset, nobody by hand; a manual start (`trigger`), anyone who can see the
record; an approval or task, refused (it needs someone, `lintErrors`).

PermissionChange.description: One permission change: who may do a node of a workflow.

note.description: What changed, shown in the version list (default "Permissions changed").

changed.description: False when the changes left everything as it was (no version was published).

draftSkipped.description: The nodes the draft no longer has, so the draft did not get their change.

recordsMoved.description: Lifecycles: how many record instances moved from earlier versions to the new one.

recordsKept.description:
Lifecycles: how many record instances stayed on an older version because its states or transitions differ from
the new one (moving them could leave them in a state that version does not have); migrate them explicitly.

key.description: Its key (unique; other workflows and the API use it).

entity.description: The record type it is about, if any.

version.description: The latest published version (0 when never published).

hasDraftChanges.description: True when the draft differs from the latest published version.

updatedAt.description: When the draft or status last changed.

runningInstances.description: Unfinished automation and record instances of any version.

PermissionsSummary.description: What `POST /definitions/{id}/permissions` did: the definition's summary plus the outcome of the change.

note.description: What changed, shown in the version list.

ReasonBody.description: A body carrying only a reason (e.g. cancelling an instance).

lifecycle.description: The key of the lifecycle that owns a field of this entity, if any.

stateEnteredAt.description: When the record entered its state, if known.

transitions.description: What the viewer may apply now.

instances.description: Recent automation runs and lifecycle child runs about the record.

manual.description: Manual workflows the viewer may start from the record.

states.description: All states of the lifecycle: `{ key, label, category, tone }`.

oneOf.description: Starting the workflow over, when the viewer may (null otherwise).

RecordView.description:
Everything a record page shows (the record panel): its lifecycle state, the transitions the viewer may
apply, open tasks, recent runs and manual starts. Reading never creates the lifecycle instance; a
record without one is shown in the state it would get.

input.description: The reset form's answers, if it has a form.

lifecycle.description: Which lifecycle, when the record has more than one.

undo.description: The reset list's item ids to take back (from `GET …/reset`); empty = none.

token.description: The reset list's token (from `GET …/reset`); when the list has changed since, the reset fails with `resetChanged`.

comment.description: The person's remarks: required when the reset's `comment` is `required` (`commentRequired`), ignored when `none`; at most 2000 characters.

id.description: Stable id to send back in the reset's `undo` list.

kind.description: `field` (a field it changed), `created` (a record it created), `action`, `message`, `webhook` or `move` (another record moved by `applyTransition`, never undoable).

title.description: What it was, in words ("Reviewer of Application “Bursary”: back to nobody").

detail.description: More about it (the value now, what created it), if any.

undoable.description: Whether the reset can take it back (messages, webhooks and actions without an undo cannot).

selected.description: Whether it is ticked by default (not when it was changed again since, or cannot be undone).

warning.description: Why it is unticked or cannot be undone, if so.

ResetItem.description: One thing a workflow did that the reset list shows (spec §6 reset).

label.description: The button label ("Reset workflow" by default).

to.description: The state key it goes back to.

confirm.description: A confirmation question to ask first, if set.

oneOf.description: The form to fill in (e.g. a reason), if the reset asks for one.

comment.description: Whether the person is asked for remarks: `none`, `optional` or `required` (resolved, never null).

ResetOption.description: Starting the record's workflow over, offered to the people the lifecycle's reset allows (spec §6).

reset.description: The reset as offered to the viewer.

items.description: What the record's workflows did since it last started over, oldest first.

token.description:
Fingerprint of the items and the values they would restore. Send it back with the reset: when the list has
changed since (someone edited a field it would restore), the reset fails with `resetChanged`.

ResetPreview.description: What a reset would do: its option (label, target, form) and the workflow's work it can take back.

target.description: Which incident, by token id or failed step id, when several paths stopped (default: the first).

specVersion.description: The spec version the engine implements.

registry.description: What workflows may read, watch, write and call.

SeqGap.description: A range of sequence numbers a purge deleted on purpose.

revision.description: The revision they were based on (optimistic concurrency).
Their revision, to send back with `PUT /settings`.

entity.description: The record's entity, if the signal is about one.
The record type it is about; null = no record.

SignalDescriptor.description: A named event the app raises, optionally about one record type.

resumed.description: How many waiting workflows the signal resumed.

definition.description: The definition to run (usually the draft).

oneOf.description: The record, trigger and events of the test run.

SimulationEntry.description: One thing that happened (or would have happened) during a test run.

type.description: `decide` (an open task), `advance` (move the clock), `signal`, `set` (change record fields).

step.description: For `decide`: the step of the task (defaults to the first open task).

data.description: For `decide`: the form answers; for `signal`: the signal data.

user.description: For `decide`: who decides (defaults to the task's first undecided assignee).

signal.description: For `signal`: the signal key, raised for the test record.

values.description: For `set`: the record fields to change (a committed change, so triggers and condition waits react).

SimulationEvent.description: One thing to do during a test run, after the workflow starts.

entityId.description: The real record to read (its values are read, never written).

values.description: Record values to use instead of (or on top of) the real record's.

trigger.description: Automations: the change that starts it (`field`, `from`, `to`), or signal/manual data.

fromState.description: Lifecycles: the state the record is in, and the transition to try.

transition.description: Lifecycles: the transition key to apply (who is not checked in test runs).

input.description: Form answers: the transition's input or the manual trigger's form.

events.description: What happens after the start, in order (at most int WorkflowEngine.MaxSimulationEvents).

SimulationRequest.description: What a test run (`POST /simulate`) should do: which record to use, how the workflow starts and what happens next (at most 50 events).

problems.description: Lint problems of the definition (errors stop the run before it starts), plus a `lifecycleNotSelected` warning when the test record would not get this lifecycle.

log.description: What happened, side effects that were skipped included (messages, webhooks, actions, writes).

instances.description: The instances the run created, oldest first.

openTasks.description: Tasks still open at the end.

record.description: The test record's values at the end (masked, readable fields only).

error.description: Why the run stopped early, if it did.

SimulationResult.description: What a test run did. Everything is masked like the audit log; fields workflows may not read are left out.

outputs.description: Outputs to give the skipped step.

target.description: Which incident, by token id or failed step id, when several paths stopped (default: the first).

outputs.description: The outputs later steps can read.

StepDescriptor.description: A step type the builder can offer.

id.description: The step record's id (one per attempt).

nodeId.description: The step's id in the definition.

title.description: The step's title in the definition version the instance runs, if it has one.

attempt.description: The attempt number (1 for the first try, higher after retries).

status.description: One of StepStatus: running, waiting, completed, failed, skipped, cancelled.

input.description: What the step was given (recipients, URL, action input…).

error.description: Why the attempt failed, if it did.

endedAt.description: When it ended, or null while it runs or waits.

StepView.description: One executed step of an instance, as the run viewer shows it (inputs, outputs and errors are masked, spec §11).

data.description: Their form answers, if the task has a form (masked in views).

TaskDecision.description: One person's decision on a task.

instanceId.description: The instance whose step created it.

instructions.description: The rendered instructions template, if any.

entity.description: The record type it is about, if any.

entityTitle.description: The record's title when the task was created.

assigneeNames.description: Their names, in the same order.

rule.description: For approvals: `{ type, value }` (spec §7 assignee rules).

oneOf.description: The form to fill in when deciding, if any.

requireComment.description: `never`, `reject` (an approval's `rejected`, or a task outcome whose tone is `danger`, needs a comment) or `always`.

allowDelegation.description: Whether an assignee may hand it to someone else.

outcome.description: The settled outcome, once there is one.

overdue.description: True while open past its due time.

escalationLevel.description: How many times it has been escalated.

completedAt.description: When it was settled, cancelled or timed out.

canDecide.description: True when the viewer is an assignee who has not decided yet and the task is open.

TaskView.description: An approval or task waiting for (or decided by) people, as the inbox and record panel show it. Decision answers are masked.

stepId.description: The step it is at, if any.

TokenView.description: One thread of an instance: parallel paths and parallel forEach items each run in their own.

lifecycle.description: Which lifecycle, when the entity has more than one.

comment.description: The person's remarks: required when the transition's `comment` is `required` (`commentRequired`), ignored when `none`; at most 2000 characters.

confirm.description: A confirmation question to ask first, if set.

oneOf.description: The input form to fill in, if the transition asks for one.

comment.description: Whether the person is asked for remarks: `none`, `optional` or `required` (resolved, never null).

TransitionOption.description: A transition the viewer may apply to a record now (its `who` and guard hold, spec §6).

type.description: The trigger type (spec §5), or `lifecycle` for an owned field.

entity.description: The record type it watches, if any.

field.description: The field it watches or owns, if any.

summary.description: A plain-English description ("When Application Stage changes to Done").

version.description: The published version the trigger comes from.

TriggerOverview.description: One active trigger or lifecycle, for the "Watching" section of global settings.

oneOf.description: Extra data: lint problems for `lintErrors`, field errors for `invalidInput`.

WorkflowError.description: The body of every error response: a stable code (spec), a message for people, and details (lint problems, form errors…).

specVersion.description: The spec version of the registry format (currently `1`).

entities.description: The record types workflows may be about, with their fields.

signals.description: Named events the app raises (`signal` triggers and waits).

WorkflowRegistry.description:
Everything the host app lets workflows read, watch, write and call (spec §2). Served to the
builder at `GET /schema`; definitions may only reference what is listed here.

id.description: The user id assignees and actors use.

email.description: Where email notifications go, if any.

roles.description: Role keys the person has (registry roles).

groups.description: Group keys the person belongs to (registry groups).

WorkflowUser.description: A person the app's directory knows.
